title: Binary makes use of insecure API(s)
description: The binary may contain the following insecure API(s) _fopen , _memcpy , _sscanf , _strlen (MobSF section: binary)
remediation: Review the finding in the MobSF report and fix the cause, or suppress it with a reason and an expiry date.

title: Binary makes use of malloc function
description: The binary may use _malloc function instead of calloc (MobSF section: binary)
remediation: Review the finding in the MobSF report and fix the cause, or suppress it with a reason and an expiry date.

title: Application binary has rpath set
description: The binary has Runpath Search Path (@rpath) set. In certain cases an attacker can abuse this feature to run arbitrary executable for code execution and privilege escalation. Remove the compiler option -rpath to remove @rpath. (MobSF section: macho)
remediation: Review the finding in the MobSF report and fix the cause, or suppress it with a reason and an expiry date.

title: Application binary does not have symbols stripped
description: Debug Symbols are available. To strip debugging symbols, set Strip Debug Symbols During Copy to YES, Deployment Postprocessing to YES, and Strip Linked Product to YES in project's build settings. (MobSF section: macho)
remediation: Review the finding in the MobSF report and fix the cause, or suppress it with a reason and an expiry date.

title: Tampering: Malicious or oversized input from the user
description:
The user can enter very long strings, control characters or format-string-like text. This may cause UI hangs, a crash or an unexpected greeting when the name is interpolated.

Framework stride, element 'Enter name', likelihood medium, impact low, rated low.
remediation: - Limit input length and strip control characters. Build the greeting with safe string interpolation and never use it as a format string. (ASVS V2.2.1, V1.2.1)

title: Tampering: Unvalidated name written to the Keychain
description:
The entered name is stored without length or content limits. Oversized or malformed input could corrupt the stored item or fill the store. Saves are also not tied to a specific query, so a save could overwrite an unrelated item.

Framework stride, element 'Save last name request', likelihood low, impact low, rated low.
remediation: - Validate and trim the name (maximum length, allowed characters) before saving. Use a fixed service and account key with SecItemUpdate or SecItemAdd, and check the returned OSStatus. (ASVS V2.2.1, V2.1.1)

title: Elevation of privilege: CI pipeline pinned to a mutable tag of the factory workflow
description:
The diff moves the reusable workflow reference and factory-ref from @main to @v1. A tag can be moved or retagged. Anyone who gains control of the upstream repository could run code in this repository's workflow, which has write permissions and `secrets: inherit`. That code could tamper with the app build or leak secrets.

Framework stride, element 'iOS app', likelihood low, impact high, rated medium.
remediation: - Pin the reusable workflow and factory-ref to a full commit SHA, and keep the workflow permissions minimal. Pass only the secrets the workflow needs instead of `secrets: inherit`. (ASVS V15.2.1, V13.4.1)

title: Spoofing: Substituted Keychain item on a compromised device
description:
On a jailbroken device an attacker could replace or pre-seed the Keychain item. The app would then show an attacker-chosen name as the last user. Without a Secure Enclave-backed access control the app cannot tell the value was not written by itself.

Framework stride, element 'Keychain', likelihood low, impact low, rated low.
remediation: - Set an access control on the item and treat the stored value as non-authoritative display data. Optionally detect jailbreak and warn the user. (ASVS V14.3.3, V11.3.1)

title: Repudiation: No record of stored-name changes or Keychain errors
description:
The app does not log when the stored name is saved or cleared, or when Keychain operations fail. Failed or unexpected writes cannot be investigated afterwards. This is low risk for a single-user local app.

Framework stride, element 'iOS app', likelihood low, impact low, rated low.
remediation: - Log Keychain operation outcomes (status codes only, with no name value) through the unified logging system. (ASVS V16.3.2, V16.2.1)

title: Denial of service: Crash or hang on Keychain failure or bad input
description:
The app may crash or block the main thread when a Keychain call fails (for example when the device is locked or an item is missing) or when it receives very large input. The user then cannot use the app.

Framework stride, element 'iOS app', likelihood low, impact low, rated low.
remediation: - Handle every OSStatus error without force-unwrapping. Run Keychain calls off the main thread and show a safe default state on failure. (ASVS V16.5.1, V16.5.2)

title: Information disclosure: Name exposed through logs, screenshots or the app switcher
description:
The greeting and last name are shown on screen. They can be written to system logs, captured in app-switcher snapshots, or exposed to the pasteboard or keyboard cache. Other parties on the device could then read them.

Framework stride, element 'Show greeting and last name', likelihood medium, impact low, rated low.
remediation:
- Do not log the name. Use os_log privacy markers (.private) if logging is needed. (ASVS V14.2.4, V16.2.5)
- Mark the input field as non-autocorrecting and hide or blur the content when the app moves to the background. (ASVS V14.3.3)

title: Tampering: Loaded Keychain value trusted without validation
description:
A value read back from the Keychain could have been altered on a jailbroken device or by another process. If the app uses it without validation or decodes it unsafely, it could be displayed or processed in a harmful way.

Framework stride, element 'Load last name response', likelihood low, impact low, rated low.
remediation: - Treat the loaded value as untrusted. Decode it as UTF-8 with a length limit, fall back to an empty state on failure, and render it only as plain text. (ASVS V2.2.1, V1.2.1)

title: Information disclosure: Stored name readable by other apps or from device backups
description:
The last entered name is a personal identifier kept in the Keychain. If the item is saved with a permissive accessibility class (such as kSecAttrAccessibleAlways) or with iCloud sync enabled, it can be read on a locked or compromised device, or from backups. A shared keychain access group could also expose it to other apps.

Framework stride, element 'Keychain', likelihood low, impact medium, rated low.
remediation:
- Store the item with kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly, no kSecAttrSynchronizable, and no shared access group. (ASVS V14.3.3, V11.3.1)
- Use the Keychain for persistent storage only. Do not copy the name to UserDefaults, files or logs. (ASVS V14.2.4, V14.3.3)
